lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.unitTitle: Body Signals and Building a Fueling Meal
lessonRef.title: Explicit model: nonjudgmental noticing

objective: Learners practice noticing and naming five body signals (hunger, thirst, tiredness, boredom, and stress) using plain, non-judgmental language, without any reference to weight, size, or calories, so they can recognize what their body is telling them before deciding how to respond.
scenario: Across one ordinary day, the learner pauses four separate times to notice what their body is signaling right then, names the signal in a private notebook using neutral words, and picks one helpful response to try for that signal without rating themselves as good or bad for having it.
safetyNotes: Notebook entries are private; a guardian may see the completion status but not the raw entries themselves.
No weight, size, calorie, or body-shape language is used anywhere in this task, by the learner or in feedback.
materials: a private notebook, index cards, or a digital note only the learner and a trusted adult can see

tasks.directions: Before the day starts, review the five signal words with your adult: hunger, thirst, tiredness, boredom, stress.

prompts.text: For each of the five signal words, write one plain-language clue your own body gives you when that signal shows up (for example, a clue for tiredness, not a definition of the word).

tasks.directions: With your adult, practice one full round: notice a signal right now, name it using a neutral word, and say one response you could try.

prompts.text: I named the signal using one of the five neutral words, not a judgment word.
I named the clue in my body that told me the signal was there.
I named one response I could try, without deciding whether the signal itself was good or bad.

tasks.directions: On your own across the rest of the day, notice and record three more separate signal moments in your private notebook.

prompts.text: For each of the three moments, record only: the signal word, the clue, and the response you tried. No score or rating.

tasks.directions: Look back over your four entries for the day.

prompts.text: Which signal was hardest to notice or name today, and what made noticing it harder than the others?

remediation: If a learner keeps reaching for a judgment word instead of a neutral signal word, reteach with a matching activity: give five neutral signal words and five example body clues on separate cards and have the learner pair them before returning to live noticing.
extension: Have the learner notice the same signal at two different times of day and compare, in writing, whether the clue or the helpful response changed between the two moments.
